covers.quote: Some words only work with specific prepositions
Some words only work with specific prepositions.
Not all prepositions work for every word or phrase.
For example, 'different' is always followed by 'to' or 'from', but not by 'than'.

rules.quote: Some words are always followed by particular prepositions.
rules.specification: The page explicitly accepts ‘different to/from’ and rejects ‘different than’. Its examples also accept ‘discussion about’ and reject ‘discussion around’ when introducing the topic. It does not provide a complete inventory of acceptable combinations; broader coverage needs an agreed lexical reference. Do not interpret ‘always followed’ as requiring a preposition after every occurrence of these words.
rules.violation_condition: A word or phrase is paired with an incompatible dependent preposition, including ‘different than’ in a comparison or ‘discussion around’ introducing the topic of discussion.
when: When a word or phrase takes a dependent preposition.
The discussion example concerns the topic of the discussion, not its physical location.
rules.why: G-2/G-4: the word-specific combinations are cases of one collocation check; the heading and introductory wording restate it.
